penalties_applied.name: b2c_at_scale_needed
penalties_applied.reason: Privacy/ad-blocking tools targeting individual consumers need large user volume to generate meaningful revenue; the business model requires >1000 paying consumers to work at even minimal scale.

rationale: The buyer is individual privacy-conscious consumers — not a named business role with a budget — and while analogues like uBlock exist, AI-ad filtering is nascent enough that willingness-to-pay is speculative rather than proven. The problem is real but too early: ChatGPT ads are just launching, the technical challenge of detecting AI-generated sponsored content is genuinely hard (score 5 buildability), and consumer distribution without a clear channel makes this an uphill fight. After the b2c-at-scale penalty the total lands at 3.6, below the validate threshold. Come back in 6 months when the problem is concrete and measurable.
solution_plan: A solo non-technical operator cannot build this viably right now. Detecting AI-sponsored content reliably requires a browser extension with a classification model, which is non-trivial to build with Claude alone, and distributing it to thousands of consumers with no existing channel is a major acquisition problem. The idea is worth watching but not acting on today.
notes: Total below min_total_to_validate (3.6 < 5.5). Problem is pre-product-market-fit at this date. Re-evaluate Q4 2026 if ChatGPT ad complaints become a measurable, named complaint category.
